notes: Event date: 6 June 1944 (DANFS: entered the Baie de la Seine on the morning of 6 June, opened fire at 0552; Wikipedia agrees on 0552 and about 4,000 yards from Omaha Beach). Event definition: Arkansas took up a position 4,000 yards off Omaha Beach and opened fire on German positions around the beach, in Task Group 124.9. Event support: three source families (US Navy NHHC/DANFS, Wikipedia, Morison). Location: Omaha Beach (place PL0258) with a precision of 10 km. Location support: DANFS and Wikipedia give the distance (4,000 yards off Omaha Beach) but no bearing; the beach is an area, so no sea point is worked (the pilot used the objective at 0.3 when only a range without a bearing could be had from a point, C9426; here the sector is given and the beach stands for the operational area, as Cherbourg does for C9424 at 0.5). Review: confidence 0.5 from the rubric (approximate sea position; the sector is given by more than one family but the bearing is not, so the beach is used as the operational area (0.5)); added in the Normandy chunk 1 pass (branch normandy-wtf-ships, 16 November 2026): old value none, new value this claim; parent_unit_id old value none, new value blank, reason: parents are left blank on claim rows (the chain is in the command relations). Context: Old value none, new value Omaha Beach as the operational area, reason: a range without a bearing from an area (the beach) is not turned into a point. Commander: Capt. F. G. Richards (Morison App. I, Battle Summary 39 App. B(1), DANFS commanding-officers table).

Location support: the port is named as the objective; the ship's own position is not given (same choice as C9424 for Texas).
